data.one_liner: Run Dart code in the background using location updates on Android and iOS.
data.what_it_does: The plugin keeps a Dart isolate alive by receiving location updates even when the app is in the background or task‑killed. It streams those updates so you can execute custom logic, such as step counting or sending location to a server.
use_when: You need periodic background processing triggered by location changes
You want to monitor distance walked, steps, or arrival at a destination
Your app must continue work after the user puts it in the background
avoid_when: You need background work unrelated to location
You require execution after a full app termination on iOS without location callbacks
Battery‑critical apps that cannot afford constant location polling
strengths: Uses native location services (significant‑change on iOS, foreground service on Android)
Works even when the app is task‑killed (iOS significant‑change, Android foreground service)
weaknesses: Limited to location‑based triggers; cannot run arbitrary background tasks
Requires many permissions and native setup, impacting battery
iOS background execution only while location updates are received
data.setup_notes: Add location permissions (ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION, etc.) and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION in AndroidManifest; configure iOS Info.plist with NSLocation* keys and UIBackgroundModes (fetch, location); register DispatchEngine in AppDelegate as shown; optionally use permission_handler to request permissions.

alternatives.name: geolocator
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides location updates without the background‑service overhead; suitable if you only need foreground location tracking
